description: Assign, change, or remove the current Designate for an NCR. The same endpoint handles all three: presence of designate_id in the body assigns/replaces, absence (or null) removes.
authorization: Only the NCR's own Originator (ncr.originator_id === session user id) — not the current Designate, not QA Staff, not a Manager/Admin

id.description: MongoDB ObjectId of the NCR document

designate_id.description: User id to assign as Designate. Omit or pass null to remove the current Designate instead.

designate_name.description: Display name of the Designate, resolved client-side from the same user typeahead already used for CE/CS selection. Required when designate_id is present; ignored on removal.

designate_email.description: Email address of the Designate, resolved client-side from the same user typeahead already used for CE/CS selection (matching how ce_cs_email is already supplied on NCR creation). Required when designate_id is present — the assignment notification email (FR-006) is sent to this address; ignored on removal.

designate_id: Cannot assign the Originator as their own Designate

body.message: Only the NCR Originator can assign, change, or remove the Designate
Cannot assign, change, or remove the Designate on a Closed NCR

side_effects: On assign/change: set originator_designate_id and originator_designate_name on the NCR document; append a 'delegate.assigned' user event to ncr.events[] with payload {designate_id, designate_name}; send the Designate a notification email with a link to the NCR

On removal: clear originator_designate_id and originator_designate_name; append a 'delegate.removed' user event to ncr.events[] with payload {previous_designate_id, previous_designate_name}; no email sent
notes: Assigning a new Designate while one is already assigned replaces it — an NCR has at most one active Designate at a time
Self-assignment (designate_id === the Originator's own id) is rejected with 400, not 403 — it's an invalid request shape, not an authorization failure
The Designate's own identity (not the Originator's) is what gets recorded when they later perform a Designate-eligible action (e.g. closure) — this endpoint only manages the assignment itself
Once assigned, the Designate gains access via the existing NCR visibility/authorization checks (see data-model.md) — no separate 'accept' step exists
